question: On 29 December 2023 the Greek Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport issued Ministerial Decision 362897 on the rights of passengers using regular and occasional urban, long distance and international passenger transport1.

According to governmental statements, the initiative is supposed to be part of a package of measures to support the rights of persons with disabilities in the transport sector, purportedly enshrined in the wording of indent 1 of Article 3(1) of that ministerial decision.

2 However, in the immediately following indent, the relevant provision is, in practice, nullified through the obligation to comply with competing health and/or safety requirements (relating, in part, to EU law), as well as because of the inadequacy of vehicles and infrastructure to serve persons with disabilities.
3 Twelve years after the issue of Regulation (EU) No 181/2011, Greek land-based public transport and stops as a rule do not serve, or underserve, most groups of persons with disabilities.

At the same time, Greece consistently ranks among the worst performing Member States in accessibility and, instead of the government paying attention to the basics, it continues to legitimise the reluctance of public transport service providers to modernise infrastructure and vehicle fleets.

In doing so, it is persistently and unacceptably passing on this serious problem to persons with disabilities, who are already vulnerable and at risk of social exclusion. In view of the above, does the Commission consider that the facts set out above constitute an effective, reasonable and appropriate application or transposition of EU law (e.g.: Regulation (ΕU) No 181/2011 and Regulation (ΕU) 2021/782)?
Does it believe that the facts set out above comply with Articles 21, 26 and 38 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.6.2024) On the basis of an initial analysis, the Ministerial Decision mentioned in the Honourable Member’s question1 does not appear to be contrary the EU legislation on passenger rights. The Ministerial Decision complements the Regulation (EU) No 181/20112, by granting rights to passengers using urban transport modes other than buses.
Article 3(1) of the Ministerial Decision reflects the relevant provisions of Regulation (EU) No 181/2011.

Article 9(1) of Regulation (EU) No 181/2011 stipulates the right of persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility to use bus and coach transport, whereas Article 10(1) of this Regulation contains two derogations limiting this right to the extent strictly required for reasons of safety or of the design of the vehicles or infrastructure3.

Accordingly, carriers may refuse to transport person on the grounds of disability or of reduced mobility: (a) in order to meet applicable safety requirements established by international, Union or national law, or in order to meet health and safety requirements established by the competent authorities; (b) where the design of the vehicle or the infrastructure, including bus stops and terminals, makes it physically impossible to take on board, alight or carry the person with disability or person with reduced mobility in a safe and operationally feasible manner.
The Commission would also note that EU legislation on transport accessibility currently only covers certain modes and generally applies to new, renewed or upgraded vehicles and infrastructure4.

1 Ministerial Decision 362897 of 23 December 2023 of the Greek Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport. 2 Regulation (EU) No 181/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 February 2011 concerning the

rights of passengers in bus and coach transport and amending Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004 (OJ L 55, 28.2.2011, p. 1). 3 See recitals 7 and 8 of the Regulation. 4 Regulation (EU) No 1300/2014, OJ L 356, 12.12.2014, p. 110, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/1300/oj Regulation (EU) 2019/2144, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2019/2144/oj Directive 2009/45/EC, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A32009L0045
